subject: Bluestream tenant debug log carveout and SIG/CAIQ evidence deliverable
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@bluestreamhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: security@bluestreamhealth.com; Mark Patel <mark.patel@legal.bluestreamhealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant-level debug log carveout request + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Bluestream is mapping our compliance obligations for a pilot and we have a customer-specific ask: the pilot requires us to retain a narrow set of tenant debug traces for 90 days (instead of Redwood's default 30d ephemeral window) for forensic sampling during the trial.

Before we proceed with contract language I need two things for our InfoSec team: a filled SIG/CAIQ (we sent the request form attached) and a short write-up that explains the proposed carveout, compensating controls, and how forensics snapshots would be created and deleted.

Can Redwood provide:
- A completed SIG/CAIQ packet (or estimated delivery date)
- A one-page description of: what data would be retained, who can access it, retention TTL, deletion process and attestations
- Any SOC2 artifacts that cover retention/exposure for debug logs

Attachments: Bluestream_SIG_Request_Form.pdf (they filled out the form).

Appreciate quick confirmation of scope and timeline — our security review is on a tight calendar.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Sr. Security Program Manager
Bluestream Health

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@bluestreamhealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-26T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level debug log carveout request + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the filled form. We're happy to support a pilot carveout but will need to align on narrow scoping and controls.

Quick plan:
1) Internal review (Priyom and Ben are looped) to confirm what debug traces are product-available for a tenant-level 90d TTL.
2) We'll produce a SIG/CAIQ answer workbook (initial draft) and a 1-page forensics retention write-up for Bluestream to attach to procurement.
3) We'll include SOC2 Type II excerpt that describes our logging and retention controls; if needed we can provide a redacted attestation PDF.

Can you confirm: this carveout is strictly for tenant debug traces (no PII), limited to the pilot tenant IDs you will supply, and Bluestream wants a 90-day TTL followed by automated deletion and attestations?

If yes I will get an initial delivery ETA by EOD Tuesday (5/28).

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Manager, Security & Compliance Ops
Redwood Inference

On Tue, May 25, 2028 at 10:12 AM Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@bluestreamhealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Stephanie,
> ...
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai; Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@bluestreamhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-28T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level debug log carveout request + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Stephanie / Elena — I reviewed the request with runtime and forensics. Summary of technical boundaries:

- Scope: tenant debug traces are limited to non-PII operational traces (request headers, internal debug flags, model inference IDs). We will not retain full user prompts or embeddings.
- Isolation: carveout will be tenant-scoped; only a customer-designated tenant_id namespace will be persisted beyond 30d into a separate short-lived storage bucket with restricted IAM.
- Access controls: access limited to SRE on-call + authorized incident responders; access requires documented justification + time-bound signed link.
- Retention flow: retained data TTL = 90 days; deletion job runs nightly and emits a deletion event to our audit log. We can provide a verifiable deletion manifest for each purge cycle.
- Forensics snapshot process: on request we can produce a snapshot package (redacted for any accidental PII) and provide a signed manifest plus hash; process doc attached.

ETA: I can produce the SIG workbook answers and a one-page forensics write-up by 2028-05-30 EOD. Ben, any SOC2 attestation notes to add?

Attachment: forensics-snapshot-process.docx

Regards,
Priyom Das
Staff Engineer, Runtime & Forensics
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai; stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai; Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@bluestreamhealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level debug log carveout request + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Elena / team — quick SOC2 note: our Type II report covers log management, access controls, and secure deletion processes. I am attaching a redacted excerpt that specifically references retention and deletion controls for ephemeral telemetry. We typically don't include tenant-specific carveouts in the public report, but we can provide a customer-facing attestation letter that states:

- Redwood will implement the 90d tenant-scoped retention for the pilot tenant IDs provided by Bluestream.
- Deletion will be automated and auditable; we will provide deletion manifests on request.

If Bluestream needs an executed attestation we will need a simple MSA addendum and a brief security addendum. I can draft the attestation template after we finalize the SIG answers.

Attachment: SOC2-Type2-attestation.pdf (redacted excerpt)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@bluestreamhealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-01T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant-level debug log carveout request + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Elena — attaching the initial deliverables per our timeline.

What I'm sharing (attachments + links):
- redwood_SIG_answers_v1.xlsx — draft SIG/CAIQ answers populated from runtime & compliance teams (please treat as work-in-progress).
- forensics-snapshot-process.docx — technical runbook for snapshot creation, redaction, manifest/hash, and deletion flow.
- SOC2-Type2-attestation.pdf — redacted excerpt relevant to log retention controls.
- Note: We received Bluestream_SIG_Request_Form.pdf from you earlier and have used it to prioritize sections.

Next steps we propose:
1) Bluestream to confirm the pilot tenant IDs and acknowledge restriction to non-PII debug traces.
2) We will prepare a customer attestation letter (draft) and a single-page forensics summary for procurement.
3) If acceptable we can route a short MSA addendum (security addendum) through legal — I will attach the draft to HS-89027 in HubSpot.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDexample (working folder with source docs).

If you want a short workshop to walk your InfoSec through the forensics runbook, Ben and Priyom are available next week.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen

Redwood Inference
